recognize_zh: 成熟嗜中性球的細胞核只有兩葉，呈對稱的眼鏡狀（pince-nez）或花生狀，染色質非常粗糙團塊狀，而細胞質顆粒正常，是 Pelger-Huët 異常的典型表現。
features: Mature-sized neutrophils with bilobed nuclei forming symmetric spectacle-like (pince-nez) or peanut-shaped configurations
Markedly coarse, clumped, mature chromatin inappropriate for the degree of lobation
Normal pale cytoplasm with fine specific granules; no hypogranulation
Uniform involvement of all neutrophils in the field
Background red cells largely normocytic and normochromic
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows neutrophils of normal size whose nuclei are uniformly hyposegmented, forming bilobed pince-nez or peanut-shaped configurations with coarsely clumped, mature chromatin. The cytoplasm is normally granulated, and no dysplastic hypogranulation is seen. Red cells are essentially unremarkable. In a patient without myelodysplasia or drug exposure, findings are consistent with congenital Pelger-Huët anomaly (LBR mutation).

ddx.vs: Acquired pseudo-Pelger cells usually affect only a subset of neutrophils and are accompanied by cytoplasmic hypogranulation, cytopenias and other dysplastic features, whereas congenital PHA involves nearly all neutrophils with normal granulation.
Agents such as mycophenolate, taxanes, valproate or tacrolimus cause reversible hyposegmentation with a temporal drug association; morphology alone may be indistinguishable.
Bands have a non-segmented horseshoe nucleus with less condensed chromatin, and are accompanied by toxic granulation or Döhle bodies in infection.
Immature precursors have round or kidney-shaped nuclei with finer chromatin and more basophilic cytoplasm, not symmetric bilobed nuclei with dense chromatin.
